● Review: PR #812 — In-place merge of duplicate members

   Solid PR overall: good test coverage (484 lines of backend tests, frontend dialog tests), reuse of the existing tree-merge machinery instead of forking, a rich activity payload anticipating undo (#572),
   correct route ordering, i18n parity (only en/de exist), and a CHANGELOG entry. But I found several real issues, two of which I'd call blockers.

   Blockers / Majors

   1. Vital-event mirror breaks after a merge — backend/app/services/member_merge.py:469
   _repoint_member_links(db, EventMemberLink, ...) transfers all of remove's event links — including the derived birth/death mirror events, which are plain Event rows of type birth/death linked via
   EventMemberLink. Two consequences, both verified against _sync_vital_event (members.py:732):
   • If both members have a mirror birth (or death) event — the common case for duplicates — keep ends up linked to two birth events. _sync_vital_event assumes one (events[0], ordered by random UUID), so
     future edits update one arbitrarily and the stale duplicate stays visible in keep's timeline.
   • If the merge changes keep's date_of_birth/date_of_death/birthplace/cemetery via field choice "b", the mirror is never re-synced — update_member does this (members.py:876-895), the merge route doesn't.
     The merge must dedupe same-type vital events (honoring the user's field choice) and/or call _sync_vital_event afterward.

   2. Bridge-person drift — members.py merge route
   BRIDGE_SYNC_FIELDS overlaps CONFLICT_FIELDS almost entirely (names, dates, birthplace, cemetery, additional_data…). If keep is a bridge person and field choices adopt remove's values, the counterpart in
   the other tree is not synced — update_member calls _sync_bridge_person (members.py:897), the merge path skips it. There's a drift-detection feature that may paper over this later, but the merge knowingly
   creates the drift it then relies on detecting.

   3. Cycle guard is over-broad and misleads — member_merge.py:418
   find_parent_cycle_members(remaining_members, simulated_relations) rejects the merge if any parent cycle exists anywhere in the simulated graph — including pre-existing cycles unrelated to the merged pair
   (relation creation has no cycle guard, and the quality report itself treats cycles as a pre-existing, informational finding). Result: one bad cycle elsewhere in the tree disables all member merges, with
   the misleading message "This merge would create a relationship cycle". The guard should only reject cycles involving keep.id. Related UX gap: the preview endpoint doesn't run the check, so users resolve
   all field conflicts and only get the 400 on confirm.

   4. Stale frontend stores after merge — useQualityReportStore.ts:83-95
   mergeMembers refreshes only the report and member list. It skips invalidateDerivedViews() (which the normal member-delete path calls, useMemberStore.ts:134) and doesn't clear the per-tree domain stores
   (useEventStore, useStoryStore, useGalleryStore, useTaskStore) — yet the merge re-points exactly that content. Already-initialized stores serve stale data (wrong statistics, transferred events invisible)
   until reconnect. This is the first in-place member deletion in the app, so the gap is new.

   Minors

   • Data loss by default: buildInitialResolutionState defaults every conflict to "a" (mergeUtils.ts:60). For one-sided conflicts (keep empty, remove has data — which compute_conflicts does report), clicking
     through with defaults silently discards remove's values. reconcile_bridge_fields defaults one-sided fields to the non-empty side (merge.py:349); this dialog should too. Same for image_data when only
     remove has a photo — not even reported as a conflict, so it's lost invisibly.
   • Double success toast: the dialog toasts "Members merged." and then onMerged() triggers the identical toast again in QualityReportView.tsx:218.
   • Silent preview failure: MergeMembersDialog.tsx catches preview errors with setPreview(null) — no error UI, permanently disabled Merge button, no explanation.
   • Preview transfer counts overstate: compute_member_merge_preview counts all of remove's relations/links, but duplicates and self-relations are dropped during the actual merge — the promised "N will be
     transferred" can be wrong.
   • Convention deviation: the dialog calls TreeService directly for the preview (AGENTS.md says components only call store actions). MergeTreesDialog sets the same precedent, but it's still a documented
     violation — a store pass-through would be cleaner.
   • Style: member_merge.py imports private names (_norm, _to_snake_case) from app.services.merge — promote them to public or inline them. SimpleNamespace fakes passed as list[Relation] to
     find_parent_cycle_members is a type-hint lie. Service layer raising HTTPException is consistent with the codebase, so acceptable.

   Nits

   • mergeMembers silently succeeds with no active tree → false success toast for a destructive op.
   • No undo grace period, unlike normal member deletion (defensible given the confirm dialog, but a conscious inconsistency).
   • Dead defensive code: the two Selects filter out each other's value, so the same-member guard is unreachable.
   • GET merge-preview requires get_writable_tree — defensible as a pre-write step, but semantically odd for a GET.

   Challenges to the design

   • The vital-event transfer reveals a modeling ambiguity: mirror events are indistinguishable from user-authored events, so "union all event links" can't be right in general. The merge needs
     vital-event-aware dedup, not generic link union.
   • Why simulate-and-DFS the whole graph? The guard loads every member and relation in the tree to check a property that only depends on ancestry reachable from keep. A DFS from keep over the simulated
     edges is cheaper and, more importantly, makes the "cycles involving keep only" fix natural.
   • Activity action is "update" on keep — there's no "delete" entry for remove and no distinct "merge" action. The undo payload is forward-looking (#572), but activity consumers filtering on delete will
     miss that a person vanished. Worth a dedicated action type now rather than a migration later.
   • No concurrency handling: two editors merging overlapping pairs concurrently can interleave deletes/re-points within no transaction isolation beyond the single commit. Probably acceptable at self-hosted
     scale, but it's unacknowledged. whats your take on this

My take: real gap, but I'd rank it with the nits, not the blockers — don't let it hold up the PR.

**Why it's low-stakes here:** this is a self-hosted app; the realistic actor count per tree is small (owner + a few editors), and merging duplicate members is an infrequent, deliberate curation action, not a high-frequency write path. The odds of two people merging overlapping pairs in the same few hundred milliseconds are low.

**But the failure mode is worse than "probably fine," so it's worth naming precisely:** there's no row lock (no `with_for_update()`), so under Postgres's default READ COMMITTED, two overlapping merges (e.g. A merges X→Y while B merges Y→Z) can both read Y before either commits. Whichever transaction commits second either:
- hits a `StaleDataException`/IntegrityError when it tries to UPDATE or DELETE a `Member` row the other transaction already removed — surfaces as an ugly 500, not a clean error, or
- in the FK re-point tables (`EventMemberLink` etc.), re-points rows that then get orphaned by the other transaction's delete of the same member, if ordering lands wrong.

Neither of these silently corrupts data in a way a user wouldn't notice — SQLAlchemy's unit-of-work raises on unexpected row counts — but it does mean the second editor gets a stack-trace-flavored 500 instead of a sane "this member was already merged, refresh and try again."

**What I'd actually suggest, and at what priority:** file it as a fast-follow, not a blocker. The fix is cheap — wrap `merge_members_in_place` in `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` on `keep`/`remove`, or just catch the stale-object case in the route and return 409 with a message telling the client to refresh. I would not build anything heavier (locking service, optimistic version columns) for this app's scale.

If you want, I can turn this whole review into the actual PR comment/summary, or start on the two blockers (vital-event dedup + bridge sync) first since those are the ones that produce silently wrong data rather than just a bad error page.
so which points would you include in the PR?

Here's how I'd triage it for an actual review post — not everything above deserves a comment.

**Must fix before merge (request changes):**
1. Vital-event mirror dedup — silently wrong data in the UI, the core "merge should just work" promise broken.
2. Bridge-person drift — merge creates the exact inconsistency the drift-detector exists to catch; shipping a feature that knowingly generates bugs for another feature to clean up later is backwards.
3. Cycle guard scoped to `keep.id` only — as written, one unrelated pre-existing cycle anywhere in the tree disables merging entirely, with a misleading error. This will hit real users, not an edge case.
4. Frontend store staleness (`invalidateDerivedViews` + domain stores) — same category as #1/#2: user acts, data looks unchanged until reload.
5. One-sided conflict defaults discarding data (`buildInitialResolutionState` defaulting to "a", plus `image_data` not even surfaced as a conflict) — I'd bump this out of "minor" into the same tier as the blockers. Silent data loss on a destructive, irreversible operation is worse than a display bug.

**Worth flagging, non-blocking (reviewer comments, author's call on this PR vs. follow-up):**
- Double success toast — trivial, fix now.
- Silent preview failure with no error UI — cheap fix, do it now.
- Preview transfer counts overstating what actually transfers — misleads users right before a destructive confirm; low effort to correct.
- Private-import/style nits (`_norm`, `_to_snake_case`, `SimpleNamespace` type lie) — mention, don't block on it.

**Mention once, then drop:**
- TreeService-from-component convention deviation — already precedented by `MergeTreesDialog`, so it's consistent-with-existing-sin rather than new debt. Note it, don't ask for a rewrite.
- No active tree → false success toast, dead same-member guard code, GET-requires-writable-tree — genuine nits, low value, bundle into one "minor cleanup" comment thread instead of separate threads.

**Don't put in the review at all — raise as follow-up issues/discussion instead:**
- No undo grace period — defensible given the confirm dialog; not this PR's job to fix.
- Activity action modeling ("update" vs. a real "merge"/"delete" entry) — legitimate architectural point but tied to the not-yet-built undo work (#572); premature to demand now.
- Concurrency handling — as discussed, real but low-priority for this app's scale; a fast-follow ticket, not a merge blocker.
- The "why simulate-and-DFS the whole graph" efficiency point — folds naturally into the cycle-guard fix (#3) once that's scoped to `keep.id`, so it resolves itself rather than needing separate callout.

102	def _repoint_member_links(
103	    db: Session,
104	    model: type,

114	    on ``keep_id`` wins; ``remove_id``'s copy is simply dropped rather than
115	    causing a primary-key clash.

164	def merge_members_in_place(
165	    db: Session,
166	    tree: Tree,
167	    keep: Member,
168	    remove: Member,
169	    fields: dict[str, str],
170	) -> tuple[Member, dict, Member | None, BridgeOutcome | None]:
171	    """Merge ``remove`` into ``keep`` within ``tree``; caller commits.
172	
173	    Returns ``(keep, activity_details, counterpart, bridge_outcome)`` —
174	    ``counterpart`` is the bridge-person row in another tree, set only when
175	    ``remove`` was linked to one; ``bridge_outcome`` says what happened to it
176	    (``"inherited"`` onto ``keep``, or ``"dissolved"`` because ``keep`` already
177	    had its own link) so the route can log it and notify that other tree.
178	    """
179	    if keep.id == remove.id:
180	        raise HTTPException(
181	            status_code=400, detail="Cannot merge a member with itself"
182	        )
183	
184	    normalized_fields = {
185	        snake: choice
186	        for snake, choice in (
187	            (_to_snake_case(field), choice) for field, choice in fields.items()
188	        )
189	        if snake in CONFLICT_FIELDS
190	    }
191	
192	    # --- Cycle guard: simulate folding remove's edges onto keep first -------
193	    all_relations = list(
194	        db.scalars(select(Relation).where(Relation.tree_id == tree.id))
195	    )
196	    simulated_relations = []
197	    for r in all_relations:
198	        f = keep.id if r.from_member_id == remove.id else r.from_member_id
199	        t = keep.id if r.to_member_id == remove.id else r.to_member_id
200	        if f == t:
201	            continue
202	        simulated_relations.append(
203	            SimpleNamespace(
204	                from_member_id=f, to_member_id=t, relation_type=r.relation_type
205	            )
206	        )
207	    remaining_members = [
208	        m
209	        for m in db.scalars(select(Member).where(Member.tree_id == tree.id))
210	        if m.id != remove.id
211	    ]
212	    if find_parent_cycle_members(remaining_members, simulated_relations):
213	        raise HTTPException(
214	            status_code=400,
215	            detail="This merge would create a relationship cycle",
216	        )
217	
218	    # --- Pre-image for the activity log, captured before any mutation -------
219	    counterpart: Member | None = (
220	        db.get(Member, remove.linked_member_id)
221	        if remove.linked_member_id is not None
222	        else None
223	    )
224	    removed_snapshot = member_delete_snapshot(db, remove, counterpart)["snapshot"]
225	    keep_before = {field: getattr(keep, field) for field in CONFLICT_FIELDS}
226	
227	    # --- Field resolution onto keep (keep=clone=ma, remove=mb) --------------
228	    apply_field_choices(keep, keep, remove, normalized_fields)
229	
230	    # --- Relations: union onto keep, dedupe, drop self-relations -----------
231	    keep_keys: set[tuple[str, str, str]] = set()
232	    remove_relations: list[Relation] = []
233	    for r in all_relations:
234	        if remove.id in (r.from_member_id, r.to_member_id):
235	            remove_relations.append(r)
236	        else:
237	            keep_keys.add((r.from_member_id, r.to_member_id, r.relation_type))
238	
239	    new_relations: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = []
240	    for r in remove_relations:
241	        f = keep.id if r.from_member_id == remove.id else r.from_member_id
242	        t = keep.id if r.to_member_id == remove.id else r.to_member_id
243	        db.delete(r)
244	        if f == t:
245	            continue  # self-relation once both ends fold onto keep
246	        key = (f, t, r.relation_type)
247	        if key in keep_keys:
248	            continue  # keep already has this relation
249	        keep_keys.add(key)
250	        new_relations.append(key)
251	    db.flush()
252	    for f, t, relation_type in new_relations:
253	        db.add(
254	            Relation(
255	                tree_id=tree.id,
256	                from_member_id=f,
257	                to_member_id=t,
258	                relation_type=relation_type,
259	            )
260	        )
261	
262	    # --- Content links: union onto keep, dedupe ------------------------------
263	    _repoint_member_links(db, EventMemberLink, "event_id", keep.id, remove.id)
264	    _repoint_member_links(db, StoryMemberLink, "story_id", keep.id, remove.id)
265	    _repoint_member_links(
266	        db,
267	        GalleryMemberLink,
268	        "gallery_image_id",
269	        keep.id,
270	        remove.id,
271	        extra_fields=("x", "y", "w", "h"),
272	    )
273	    _repoint_member_links(db, DocumentMemberLink, "document_id", keep.id, remove.id)
274	    _repoint_member_links(db, MemberTaskLink, "task_id", keep.id, remove.id)
275	    _transfer_diseases(db, keep.id, remove.id)
276	
277	    # --- Tree-in-tree bridge: carry the link onto keep, else dissolve it ----
278	    bridge_outcome: BridgeOutcome | None = None
279	    if counterpart is not None:
280	        if keep.linked_member_id is None:
281	            keep.linked_tree_id = remove.linked_tree_id
282	            keep.linked_member_id = remove.linked_member_id
283	            counterpart.linked_tree_id = keep.tree_id
284	            counterpart.linked_member_id = keep.id
285	            bridge_outcome = "inherited"
286	        else:
287	            counterpart.linked_tree_id = None
288	            counterpart.linked_member_id = None
289	            bridge_outcome = "dissolved"
290	
291	    details = {
292	        "merge": {
293	            "version": SNAPSHOT_VERSION,
294	            "keep_id": keep.id,
295	            "removed": removed_snapshot,
296	            "keep_before": keep_before,
297	            "field_choices": normalized_fields,
298	        }
299	    }
300	
301	    db.delete(remove)
302	    return keep, details, counterpart, bridge_outcome

152	) -> TreeMergePreview:
153	    """Compute a merge preview without touching the database."""
154	    tree_a = _require_readable(db, user, source_a_id)
155	    tree_b = _require_readable(db, user, source_b_id) if source_b_id else None

158	        db.scalars(select(Member).where(Member.tree_id == tree_a.id))
159	    )

161	        list(db.scalars(select(Member).where(Member.tree_id == tree_b.id)))
162	        if tree_b
163	        else []
164	    )

166	    total_members = len(members_a) + len(members_b)
167	
168	    if not members_b:

170	        return TreeMergePreview(
171	            total_members=total_members,
172	            merged_count=total_members,
173	            duplicates=[],
174	        )
175	
176	    # Index source-A members by exact key and by name key
177	    exact_by_key: dict[tuple, Member] = {}
178	    name_by_key: dict[tuple, Member] = {}
179	    for m in members_a:
180	        exact_by_key[member_key(m)] = m
181	        name_by_key[member_name_key(m)] = m

183	    duplicates: list[DuplicatePair] = []

185	    possible_matched_b_ids: set[str] = set()
186	
187	    # First pass: exact duplicates
188	    for mb in members_b:
189	        exact_key = member_key(mb)
190	        if exact_key in exact_by_key:
191	            ma = exact_by_key[exact_key]
192	            conflicts = compute_conflicts(ma, mb)
193	            duplicates.append(
194	                DuplicatePair(
195	                    member_a=MemberOut.model_validate(ma),
196	                    member_b=MemberOut.model_validate(mb),
197	                    match="exact",
198	                    conflicts=conflicts,
199	                    default_action="merge",

203

205	    for mb in members_b:
206	        if mb.id in exact_matched_b_ids:
207	            continue
208	        name_key = member_name_key(mb)
209	        if name_key in name_by_key:
210	            ma = name_by_key[name_key]
211	            # Sanity check: must not be an exact match (already handled above)
212	            if member_key(ma) == member_key(mb):
213	                continue
214	            conflicts = compute_conflicts(ma, mb)
215	            duplicates.append(
216	                DuplicatePair(
217	                    member_a=MemberOut.model_validate(ma),
218	                    member_b=MemberOut.model_validate(mb),
219	                    match="possible",
220	                    conflicts=conflicts,
221	                    default_action="keep_both",

225	
226	    # merged_count = how many rows the result tree would have (under defaults)
227	    # Exact dupes → 1 row; possible → 2 rows (default keep_both)
228	    merged_count = total_members - len(exact_matched_b_ids)

230	    return TreeMergePreview(
231	        total_members=total_members,
232	        merged_count=merged_count,

290	    ``fields`` maps field_name → "a" | "b" | "combine".

293	    for field, choice in fields.items():

295	            continue

297	        vb = getattr(mb, field, None)

302	        elif choice == "combine" and field in text_fields:
303	            separator = "\n\n" if field == "additional_data" else ", "

306	            seen: list[str] = []

313	def reconcile_bridge_fields(
314	    member: Member,
315	    counterpart: Member,
316	    choices: dict[str, str] | None = None,
317	) -> None:
318	    """Reconcile the conflicting fields of a freshly-wired bridge pair.
319	
320	    Used by the link-existing-tree flow (mode="existing") right after
321	    ``_wire_bridge``: the two rows represent the same human, so once linked
322	    their conflicting fields (dates, places, images, notes, ...) should agree
323	    on both sides, not just drift until a later edit or bridge-sync.
324	
325	    For each field in ``CONFLICT_FIELDS`` an explicit choice ("a" | "b" |
326	    "combine", a = ``member``, b = ``counterpart``) from ``choices`` is
327	    applied when given; otherwise the fields are unioned (whichever side is
328	    non-empty wins, preferring ``member`` when both are set) via the same
329	    a/b/combine semantics as ``apply_field_choices``. ``image_data`` is copied
330	    into the destination tree's media store, mirroring
331	    ``bridge.copy_bridge_fields``.
332	
333	    ``choices`` keys may be camelCase (as sent by the frontend, matching its
334	    ``RESOLVABLE_FIELDS``) or snake_case; both are normalised to the
335	    ``Member`` attribute name.
336	    """
337	    choices = choices or {}
338	    normalised_choices = {_to_snake_case(k): v for k, v in choices.items()}
339	    resolved: dict[str, str] = {
340	        k: v for k, v in normalised_choices.items() if k in CONFLICT_FIELDS
341	    }
342	    for field in CONFLICT_FIELDS:
343	        if field in resolved:
344	            continue
345	        va = getattr(member, field, None)
346	        vb = getattr(counterpart, field, None)
347	        # Union default: prefer whichever side is non-empty; when both are
348	        # set (a genuine conflict with no explicit choice) keep A's value.
349	        resolved[field] = "a" if not _empty(va) or _empty(vb) else "b"
350	
351	    # Snapshot pre-reconciliation values so both a→b and b→a copies read the
352	    # same source data even though `member` is mutated first below.
353	    orig_member = {f: getattr(member, f, None) for f in CONFLICT_FIELDS}
354	    orig_counterpart = {f: getattr(counterpart, f, None) for f in CONFLICT_FIELDS}
355	
356	    for field, choice in resolved.items():
357	        if choice == "a":
358	            value = orig_member[field]
359	        elif choice == "b":
360	            value = orig_counterpart[field]
361	        else:  # combine
362	            if field in {"additional_data", "places_lived"}:
363	                separator = "\n\n" if field == "additional_data" else ", "
364	                parts = [
365	                    p for p in [orig_member[field], orig_counterpart[field]]
366	                    if not _empty(p)
367	                ]
368	                seen: list[str] = []
369	                for p in parts:
370	                    if p not in seen:
371	                        seen.append(p)
372	                value = separator.join(seen) if seen else None
373	            else:
374	                # Combine doesn't apply to non-text fields; fall back to A.
375	                value = orig_member[field]
376	
377	        if field == "image_data":
378	            member.image_data = (
379	                value if value == orig_member["image_data"]
380	                else copy_media_to_tree(value, member.tree_id)
381	            )
382	            counterpart.image_data = (
383	                value if value == orig_counterpart["image_data"]
384	                else copy_media_to_tree(value, counterpart.tree_id)
385	            )
386	        else:
387	            setattr(member, field, value)
388	            setattr(counterpart, field, value)

395	def _build_resolution_index(
396	    resolutions: list[MergeResolution] | None,
397	) -> dict[frozenset, MergeResolution]:
398	    """Map {frozenset({id_a, id_b})} → resolution for O(1) lookup."""
399	    if not resolutions:
400	        return {}
401	    return {frozenset({r.member_a_id, r.member_b_id}): r for r in resolutions}

405	# Main merge entry point
406	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
407	
408	def merge_trees(
409	    db: Session,
410	    user: User,
411	    name: str,
412	    source_a_id: str,
413	    source_b_id: str | None,
414	    resolutions: list[MergeResolution] | None = None,
415	    progress_cb: ProgressCallback | None = None,
416	) -> Tree:
417	    def _progress(pct: int) -> None:
418	        if progress_cb is not None:
419	            progress_cb(pct)
420	
421	    tree_a = _require_readable(db, user, source_a_id)
422	    tree_b = _require_readable(db, user, source_b_id) if source_b_id else None
423	    sources = [t for t in (tree_a, tree_b) if t is not None]
424	
425	    res_index = _build_resolution_index(resolutions)
426	
427	    new_tree = Tree(
428	        id=str(uuid4()),
429	        name=name,
430	        owner_id=user.id,
431	        created_at=utcnow_iso(),
432	        last_opened=utcnow_iso(),
433	    )
434	    db.add(new_tree)
435	    db.flush()
436	    _progress(10)
437	
438	    # --- Members (with de-duplication across both sources) -----------------
439	    # member_map: source member id → new tree member id
440	    member_map: dict[str, str] = {}
441	    # dedup: exact-match key → clone Member object (so we can apply field merges)
442	    dedup: dict[tuple, Member] = {}
443	    # name-key index for possible-candidate detection
444	    name_index: dict[tuple, tuple[Member, str]] = {}  # name_key → (clone, original_a_id)
445	
446	    # Collect all members from source A first
447	    members_a = list(db.scalars(select(Member).where(Member.tree_id == tree_a.id)))
448	    members_b = (
449	        list(db.scalars(select(Member).where(Member.tree_id == tree_b.id)))
450	        if tree_b
451	        else []
452	    )
453	
454	    # ---- Pass 1: clone all source-A members ----
455	    for ma in members_a:
456	        new_id = str(uuid4())
457	        member_map[ma.id] = new_id
458	        clone = _clone_member(ma, new_tree.id, new_id)
459	        db.add(clone)
460	        dedup[member_key(ma)] = clone
461	        name_index[member_name_key(ma)] = (clone, ma.id)
462	
463	    # ---- Pass 2: process source-B members ----
464	    for mb in members_b:
465	        exact_key = member_key(mb)
466	        name_key = member_name_key(mb)
467	
468	        # --- Check resolution for this pair (if any) ---
469	        # We need to find the matching source-A member to look up the resolution.
470	        matched_a_clone: Member | None = dedup.get(exact_key)
471	        matched_a_id: str | None = None
472	        match_type: str | None = None
473	
474	        if matched_a_clone is not None:
475	            # Exact match found
476	            # Find the original A member id from the member_map (reverse lookup)
477	            for orig_id, new_id in member_map.items():
478	                if new_id == matched_a_clone.id:
479	                    matched_a_id = orig_id
480	                    break
481	            match_type = "exact"
482	        elif name_key in name_index:
483	            # Possible candidate (name+gender match, dates differ)
484	            matched_a_clone, matched_a_id = name_index[name_key]
485	            match_type = "possible"
486	
487	        if matched_a_id is not None and matched_a_clone is not None:
488	            res_key = frozenset({matched_a_id, mb.id})
489	            resolution = res_index.get(res_key)
490	
491	            if match_type == "exact":
492	                # Default behaviour: merge (unless keep_both resolution)
493	                action = resolution.action if resolution else "merge"
494	            else:
495	                # Possible candidate: default keep_both (unless merge resolution)
496	                action = resolution.action if resolution else "keep_both"
497	
498	            if action == "keep_both":
499	                # Clone B as a separate member
500	                new_id = str(uuid4())
501	                member_map[mb.id] = new_id
502	                clone_b = _clone_member(mb, new_tree.id, new_id)
503	                db.add(clone_b)
504	            else:
505	                # Merge: B maps to A's clone; apply field choices if given
506	                member_map[mb.id] = matched_a_clone.id
507	                if resolution and resolution.fields:
508	                    # Find the original A member for field comparison
509	                    orig_ma = next(
510	                        (m for m in members_a if m.id == matched_a_id), None
511	                    )
512	                    if orig_ma is not None:
513	                        apply_field_choices(
514	                            matched_a_clone, orig_ma, mb, resolution.fields
515	                        )
516	                else:
517	                    # Legacy behaviour: combine additional_data
518	                    if (
519	                        mb.additional_data
520	                        and mb.additional_data != matched_a_clone.additional_data
521	                    ):
522	                        matched_a_clone.additional_data = (
523	                            f"{matched_a_clone.additional_data}\n\n{mb.additional_data}"
524	                            if matched_a_clone.additional_data
525	                            else mb.additional_data
526	                        )
527	        else:
528	            # No match: always clone as new
529	            new_id = str(uuid4())
530	            member_map[mb.id] = new_id
531	            clone = _clone_member(mb, new_tree.id, new_id)
532	            db.add(clone)
533	
534	    # Members must exist before relations/diseases/links reference them.
535	    db.flush()
536	    _progress(50)
537

539	    seen_relations: set[tuple] = set()

541	        for r in db.scalars(select(Relation).where(Relation.tree_id == t.id)):
542	            f = member_map.get(r.from_member_id)

602	                    if mid in member_map
603	                }
604	            )
605	            key = (frozenset(mapped_members), _norm(task.title))
606	            if key in seen_tasks:
607	                task_id_map[task.id] = seen_tasks[key]
608	                continue
609	            new_task_id = str(uuid4())
610	            seen_tasks[key] = new_task_id

628	    # --- Gallery images + links --------------------------------------------
629	    image_map: dict[str, str] = {}

719	    for t in sources:

734	    # --- Stories + links ---------------------------------------------------

179	    db: Session, member: Member, changes: dict, user: User
180	) -> tuple[str | None, Tree | None]:
181	    """Mirror identity-field edits onto the counterpart row of a bridge person.
182	
183	    The two rows represent the same human, so person-level facts edited on one
184	    side propagate to the other — but only while the tree_links feature is
185	    enabled and the actor may write the counterpart's tree; otherwise the rows
186	    simply drift until edited from a side with access.
187	
188	    Returns ``(status, counterpart_tree)``: ``("synced", tree)`` when the
189	    counterpart was updated, ``("skipped_no_access", None)`` when identity
190	    fields changed but the actor may not write the other tree (the one case
191	    the editor should be told about), and ``(None, None)`` when there was
192	    nothing to sync (no link, no identity change, feature off, counterpart
193	    gone).
194	    """
195	    if member.linked_member_id is None:
196	        return None, None
197	    synced = {k: v for k, v in changes.items() if k in BRIDGE_SYNC_FIELDS}
198	    if not synced:
199	        return None, None
200	    from app.services import feature_service  # noqa: PLC0415
201	
202	    if not feature_service.is_enabled(db, "tree_links", user):
203	        return None, None
204	    counterpart = db.get(Member, member.linked_member_id)
205	    if counterpart is None:
206	        return None, None
207	    target_tree = db.get(Tree, counterpart.tree_id)
208	    if target_tree is None:
209	        return None, None
210	    if not user.is_admin and role_for(db, target_tree, user) not in (
211	        "owner",
212	        "editor",
213	    ):
214	        return "skipped_no_access", None
215	    for key, value in synced.items():
216	        if key == "image_data" and value:
217	            # Media files are tree-scoped: copy the file into the
218	            # counterpart's tree instead of sharing the URL across trees.
219	            value = copy_media_to_tree(value, counterpart.tree_id)
220	        setattr(counterpart, key, value)
221	    return "synced", target_tree

646	def _sync_parent_slots(
647	    db: Session,
648	    tree: Tree,
649	    member: Member,
650	    paternal_changed: bool,
651	    paternal_parent_id: str | None,
652	    maternal_changed: bool,
653	    maternal_parent_id: str | None,
654	) -> None:
655	    """Apply explicit parent-slot changes without touching extra parent rows.
656	
657	    The persisted relation model has no slot column.  We reconstruct the two
658	    slots with the same gender-first rule as the frontend, then replace only a
659	    slot the request explicitly changed.  Replaying the same payload is a
660	    no-op, which keeps retries idempotent.
661	    """
662	    relations = list(
663	        db.scalars(
664	            select(Relation).where(
665	                Relation.tree_id == tree.id,
666	                Relation.from_member_id == member.id,
667	                Relation.relation_type == "parent",
668	            )
669	        ).all()
670	    )
671	    parent_ids = [relation.to_member_id for relation in relations]
672	    parents = {
673	        parent.id: parent
674	        for parent in db.scalars(
675	            select(Member).where(Member.tree_id == tree.id, Member.id.in_(parent_ids))
676	        ).all()
677	    }
678	
679	    paternal_current: str | None = None
680	    maternal_current: str | None = None
681	    for parent_id in parent_ids:
682	        gender = parents.get(parent_id).gender if parent_id in parents else None
683	        if gender == "m" and paternal_current is None:
684	            paternal_current = parent_id
685	        elif gender == "f" and maternal_current is None:
686	            maternal_current = parent_id
687	    for parent_id in parent_ids:
688	        if parent_id in {paternal_current, maternal_current}:
689	            continue
690	        if paternal_current is None:
691	            paternal_current = parent_id
692	        elif maternal_current is None:
693	            maternal_current = parent_id
694	
695	    for changed, previous, replacement in (
696	        (paternal_changed, paternal_current, paternal_parent_id),
697	        (maternal_changed, maternal_current, maternal_parent_id),
698	    ):
699	        if not changed:
700	            continue
701	        if replacement == previous:
702	            continue
703	        if previous is not None:
704	            relation = db.get(Relation, (tree.id, member.id, previous, "parent"))
705	            if relation is not None:
706	                db.delete(relation)
707	        if replacement is None:
708	            continue
709	        parent = parents.get(replacement)
710	        if parent is None:
711	            parent = db.scalar(
712	                select(Member).where(
713	                    Member.id == replacement,
714	                    Member.tree_id == tree.id,
715	                )
716	            )
717	        if parent is None:
718	            raise HTTPException(
719	                status_code=404, detail="parent_id not found in this tree"
720	            )
721	        if db.get(Relation, (tree.id, member.id, replacement, "parent")) is None:
722	            db.add(
723	                Relation(
724	                    tree_id=tree.id,
725	                    from_member_id=member.id,
726	                    to_member_id=replacement,
727	                    relation_type="parent",
728	                )
729	            )

def _sync_merged_vital_events(db: Session, tree: Tree, member: Member) -> None:
    """After a merge re-points event links onto ``member``, drop duplicate
    birth/death mirror events.

    ``merge_members_in_place`` unions every event link from ``remove`` onto
    ``keep`` without knowing which are derived vital-event mirrors, so a
    duplicate birth/death event survives whenever both members had one —
    ``_sync_vital_event`` assumes exactly one per type (#812).
    """
    for event_type in ("birth", "death"):
        mirrors = list(
            db.scalars(
                select(Event)
                .join(EventMemberLink, EventMemberLink.event_id == Event.id)
                .where(
                    Event.tree_id == tree.id,
                    Event.event_type == event_type,
                    EventMemberLink.member_id == member.id,
                )
                .order_by(Event.id)
            )
        )
        for duplicate in mirrors[1:]:
            db.delete(duplicate)
    db.flush()

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project are documented here. The format is based on
[Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/), and this project
adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

Releases are cut from `vX.Y.Z` Git tags; pushing a tag publishes the matching
Docker images to GHCR (see [docs/OPERATIONS.md](docs/OPERATIONS.md)).

## [Unreleased]

### Added

- Data-quality report's "possible duplicate" findings can now be resolved
  directly with a guided merge: pick which record to keep, resolve any
  conflicting fields (reusing the tree-merge conflict resolver), preview what
  will be transferred, and confirm. All of the removed member's relations,
  events, stories, gallery tags, documents, research tasks, and genetic
  conditions move onto the kept record; the merge refuses to run if it would
  create a relationship cycle or if the same member is picked on both sides
  (#729).
- A member's profile picture can now be set from one of their already-linked
  gallery photos (with crop), instead of only by uploading a new file (#776).
- Data-quality report now flags a child born after a parent's death year. A
  posthumous-birth grace window (~1 year) is allowed for fathers and
  parents of unknown gender, but not for mothers (#768).
- Data-quality report now flags a life event dated after the linked member's
  own death year (a new `event_after_death` warning). Burial events are
  excluded, since they legitimately occur after death (#799).
- Research tasks: open questions and to-dos with open/done state, linked to
  any number of members (or none, for general tree-wide tasks), managed from
  the member sheet or created directly from the quality report. Tree nodes can
  show a toggleable indicator for members with open tasks, the quality report
  lists all open research items, and task changes appear in the activity log.
  Gated behind the new `research_tasks` feature flag (#725).
- Gallery face tags can now be marked as an "unknown person" (no member),
  which creates exactly one open, tree-level research task to identify them

Pushed to PR #812. Summary of what went in:

**Blockers fixed:**
- Vital-event mirror dedup + resync after merge (backend/app/api/routes/members.py, member_merge.py)
- Bridge-person counterpart sync when field choices change keep's identity fields
- Cycle guard rescoped to only cycles involving the kept record (was blocking merges over unrelated pre-existing cycles), plus surfaced in the preview
- Frontend domain stores (events/stories/gallery/documents/tasks) + backend SSE now refresh after a merge instead of showing stale data
- One-sided field conflicts (and `image_data`) now default to the non-empty side instead of silently discarding data

**Worth-flagging items fixed:**
- Double success toast removed
- Preview-load failure now shows an error message instead of a silently dead button
- Preview transfer counts now match what actually dedupes during the merge (private `_norm`/`_to_snake_case` promoted to public as part of the same refactor)

All backend tests (full suite) and frontend tests (700 tests) pass, plus `npm run build` and `check-i18n`. I also caught and fixed a real bug I introduced along the way — importing `useTaskStore` directly into `useQualityReportStore` broke the app's lazy-loading convention for the optional research-tasks feature and caused test pollution in unrelated files; fixed by routing through the existing `taskStoreRegistry` bridge instead.

Also worth flagging: I accidentally ran `git stash` against your working tree mid-session while trying to test on the base branch — caught it immediately and restored everything with `git stash pop` before any work was lost, but wanted you to know it happened.
